From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Preliminary note on the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

Seller counsel says the [STANDARD] clauses were "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **Nothing we hold shows the Buyer agreed to any of this.** Almost every substantive point is labelled [STANDARD], and nothing is marked [OPEN]. I have treated the labels as a negotiating position and reviewed every clause on its merits. **Please confirm internally that no one on our side has agreed these positions.** If anyone has, tell me so I can adjust the analysis.

Several Seller statements also conflict with the Seller's own Disclosure Letter:

| Seller Update says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|
| Bluefen consent "addressed" | No consent obtained; conditions not shown as satisfied (para 2) |
| Riverlark released "following Completion" | Facility not repaid; no discharge (para 3) |
| Bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" | Bonuses not in funds flow; on-costs not addressed (para 5) |
| Incident "not expected to be material" | Scope, access and notification position all unknown (para 6) |
| Sandbar renewals are "ordinary-course" | Disclosure does not say they are ordinary course (para 8) |

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 30–50% cap, or 20% backed by W&I cover. The cap must apply **only** to general warranties. Fundamental, tax, specific indemnity and leakage claims sit outside it.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter at around 35%; 20% is acceptable only if W&I is in place and every carve-out below is secured.** *Reason: 20% is within market range for a clean target, but this target has several live, quantifiable risks.*

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis. AUD 250,000 basket (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated. A **tipping** basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120k), where the first dollar is recoverable once crossed. Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax, indemnity or leakage claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the deductible; counter with a tipping basket and series aggregation.** *Reason: a deductible plus a high de minimis could leave the Buyer bearing roughly AUD 250k+ of real loss.*

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims. "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 18–24 months for general warranties (24 months covers two audit cycles). Separate, longer periods for other categories.
- **Recommendation:** **Accept 18 months, or push for 24, for general warranties only. Reject the "applies to all Claims" sentence.** *Reason: the period is market, but the default-application wording silently caps every other claim category (see SPA-N-014).*

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Cap at 100% of price (AUD 24m). Time limit of at least 6 years, consistent with the NSW contract limitation period, or 7 years. No de minimis or basket. No disclosure against them.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** *Reason: if the Buyer does not get good title to 100% of the shares, it has bought nothing, so a 20% cap with an 18-month window is not a credible position.*

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that no limitation, exclusive remedy, non-reliance or knowledge qualifier applies to fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, employees or advisers. Statutory misleading-conduct rights (ACL s18) should be preserved to the extent they cannot be excluded.
- **Recommendation:** **Require an express carve-out; non-negotiable.** *Reason: courts are reluctant to read limitations as covering fraud, but relying on that invites litigation, and non-reliance clauses can undermine misrepresentation claims.*

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2). DL 1.4 adds a broad "no admission" reservation.
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure qualifies warranties only where a matter is **fairly disclosed** with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify its nature and scope. The Buyer should accept only specific disclosures against specific warranties. Disclosure must never qualify fundamental warranties, tax, indemnities or leakage. Data room disclosure, if conceded at all, should be limited to an agreed, indexed, archived USB and to fair disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject general disclosure; accept specific disclosures only, subject to a fair-disclosure standard.** *Reason: as drafted, the Buyer would bear every risk sitting anywhere in the data room, including the known issues listed here.*

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** A pro-sandbagging clause, i.e. Buyer knowledge does not reduce claims. As a fallback, silence. As a last resort, **actual** knowledge of named Buyer deal team individuals only. Never constructive knowledge, advisers' knowledge or "discoverable" matters.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete the clause; insert pro-sandbagging.** *Reason: the "discoverable" test turns due diligence into a waiver and duplicates the general disclosure problem.*

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms no consent has been obtained and the clause 11.3 conditions are not shown as satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** A **condition precedent** requiring unconditional written consent from Bluefen, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived on terms the Buyer accepts. The CP should be waivable by the Buyer only. The Seller should give a best-endeavours obligation, with a sunset date and a Buyer walk right. Add a warranty that there has been no notice of termination or adverse change.
- **Recommendation:** **Tighten into a Buyer-only CP; do not accept satisfaction on bare consent delivery.** *Reason: Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m). A consent that carries burdensome conditions, or one that ignores clause 11.3, could still destroy value.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be "released following Completion". Not repaid; no discharge in hand. Change-control clause 8.1 is likely triggered by the sale.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment **at Completion**, out of the price through the funds flow, as Debt under the debt-free mechanism. Completion deliverables should include a payout letter, a deed of release, and PPSR and any other security discharges, including any security over the Sale Shares. Add an indemnity for any residual amounts.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-Completion release; make discharge a Completion deliverable.** *Reason: a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company in default under a change-of-control clause, with security over its assets and possibly its shares.*

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of DD-005 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses, plus employer on-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, PAYG withholding mechanics, and any workers' compensation impact), treated as **Transaction Costs/Debt** and deducted from the price. They should be paid by the Company through payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the Seller. Add an uncapped specific indemnity covering claims and any later-vesting amounts.
- **Recommendation:** **Itemise in the funds flow as a price deduction, grossed up for on-costs.** *Reason: the obligation sits with the Company, which the Buyer will own, so "a matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the funds flow reflects it. True cost is likely around AUD 500k+ once on-costs are included (to be confirmed by payroll/tax advisers).*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity covers only the specific SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate". Under DD-004 clause 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **all** SOW3 fees. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** As a CP or Completion deliverable, evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. If that cannot be done before Completion, the Buyer needs a specific indemnity covering **all loss**: title failure, infringement claims, re-development or licensing costs, and customer impact. That indemnity should sit outside the cap, survive at least 6 years, and be backed by escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as inadequate; require payment plus assignment, or a broad indemnity with security.** *Reason: the real exposure is that the Company may not own IP its product depends on. The AUD 180k fee is the smallest part of that risk.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material". About 1,240 records were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notification obligations are unknown as at 22 September 2026.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenant:** complete the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches assessment (Part IIIC requires a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within 30 days). Notify the OAIC and individuals if required. Obtain a forensic or IT report. Seek deletion confirmation from the recipient. Give the Buyer access and consultation rights.
  - **Specific indemnity**, uncapped or separately capped, outside the basket and disclosure, with at least 3–4 years' survival. It should cover regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation and remediation costs, notification costs, third-party and customer claims, and Bluefen or other contract consequences.
  - **Retention or escrow** pending outcome.
  - **Warranty** that no other incidents have occurred.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the materiality characterisation; require a specific indemnity and remediation covenant.** *Reason: the assessment period appears to have run with no conclusion reached, so regulatory exposure may already exist, and the Seller has given no factual basis for "not material".*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". The Disclosure Letter says they should be "read together" but does not say whether they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Full copies and an explanation of timing and approval. In particular, the Seller should confirm whether splitting into three contracts kept each below a materiality, board-approval or conduct-of-business threshold. Also confirm whether the renewals are terminable and whether amounts are accrued. If they are not genuinely ordinary course, the cost should be treated as Leakage or Debt (a price deduction), or the contracts terminated at the Seller's cost. Add a warranty that the renewals were entered on arm's-length, ordinary-course terms with no related-party element.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the ordinary-course label without supporting evidence; reserve price adjustment.** *Reason: three identical related renewals "read together" are a classic contract-splitting pattern, and the Seller's own disclosure declines to call them ordinary course.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold treatment:
  1. general warranties
  2. fundamental warranties
  3. tax warranties and tax indemnity
  4. specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Riverlark)
  5. leakage
  6. fraud

  The default should be reversed, so general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims unless expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the default-application drafting; restructure clause 12/13 by category.** *Reason: this one sentence is what collapses every carve-out the Buyer needs into a 20% cap and 18-month regime.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012. The Seller expressly notes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Verification:** a current ASIC company extract, and a review of the constitution, share issue history and allotment records.
  - **Searches:** PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company. Confirm that no options, convertible notes, ESOP or other securities exist and that no security over the shares exists (check whether Riverlark holds share security).
  - **Fundamental warranties:** title, capacity, no encumbrances, the shares are the entire issued capital, and they are fully paid.
  - **Completion deliverables:** signed transfers, share certificates and any security releases.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on the register alone; complete independent searches and secure an uncapped title warranty.** *Reason: the Company's own register is not conclusive, and title is the core of the deal.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket, general disclosure).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** a dollar-for-dollar pre-Completion tax indemnity, not subject to disclosure, knowledge or basket, capped at 100% of price. The time limit should be at least the ATO amendment period plus a buffer (around 5–7 years). Tax warranties should be on the same extended terms.
  - **IP:** IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, assignments from employees and contractors) with an extended period of at least 3 years and a higher cap. Ironquay should be carved out separately (SPA-N-011).
- **Recommendation:** **Treat as OPEN; not settled.** *Reason: tax exposure crystallises long after 18 months, and IP is core value for an analytics business with a known IP chain gap.*

---

## Other points to keep on the list (not raised in the Seller Update)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** confirm the notification obligation is not a consent or termination trigger, and add it to Completion steps.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** confirm there is no change-of-control or indirect-assignment wording elsewhere in the contract.

## Suggested next steps
1. Reply to Seller counsel stating that no positions are agreed and all items above are open.
2. Prepare a Buyer mark-up restructuring clause 12/13 by category, with fraud, pro-sandbagging and fair-disclosure drafting.
3. Issue targeted RFIs on Bluefen clause 11.3, the Riverlark security package, the Ironquay payment, the incident timeline and forensic report, the Sandbar approvals, and DD-005 on-costs.
4. Confirm W&I appetite. The underwriter will exclude known issues (incident, Ironquay, bonuses), which reinforces the need for specific indemnities and escrow.

- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses, plus employer on-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, PAYG withholding mechanics, and any workers' compensation impact), treated as **Transaction Costs/Debt** and deducted from the price. They should be paid by the Company through payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded by the Seller. Add an uncapped specific indemnity covering claims and any later-vesting amounts.
- **Recommendation:** **Itemise in the funds flow as a price deduction, grossed up for on-costs.** *Reason: the obligation sits with the Company, which the Buyer will own, so "a matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the funds flow reflects it. True cost is likely around AUD 500k+ once on-costs are included (to be confirmed by payroll/tax advisers).*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity covers only the specific SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate". Under DD-004 clause 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of **all** SOW3 fees. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** As a CP or Completion deliverable, evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. If that cannot be done before Completion, the Buyer needs a specific indemnity covering **all loss**: title failure, infringement claims, re-development or licensing costs, and customer impact. That indemnity should sit outside the cap, survive at least 6 years, and be backed by escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as inadequate; require payment plus assignment, or a broad indemnity with security.** *Reason: the real exposure is that the Company may not own IP its product depends on. The AUD 180k fee is the smallest part of that risk.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material". About 1,240 records were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notification obligations are unknown as at 22 September 2026.

Notify the OAIC and individuals if required. Obtain a forensic or IT report. Seek deletion confirmation from the recipient. Give the Buyer access and consultation rights.

It should cover regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation and remediation costs, notification costs, third-party and customer claims, and Bluefen or other contract consequences.

  - **Warranty** that no other incidents have occurred.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". The Disclosure Letter says they should be "read together" but does not say whether they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued.

In particular, the Seller should confirm whether splitting into three contracts kept each below a materiality, board-approval or conduct-of-business threshold. Also confirm whether the renewals are terminable and whether amounts are accrued. If they are not genuinely ordinary course, the cost should be treated as Leakage or Debt (a price deduction), or the contracts terminated at the Seller's cost. Add a warranty that the renewals were entered on arm's-length, ordinary-course terms with no related-party element.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the ordinary-course label without supporting evidence; reserve price adjustment.** *Reason: three identical related renewals "read together" are a classic contract-splitting pattern, and the Seller's own disclosure declines to call them ordinary course.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold treatment:
  1. general warranties
  2. fundamental warranties
  3. tax warranties and tax indemnity
  4. specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Riverlark)
  5. leakage
  6. fraud

  The default should be reversed, so general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims unless expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the default-application drafting; restructure clause 12/13 by category.** *Reason: this one sentence is what collapses every carve-out the Buyer needs into a 20% cap and 18-month regime.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012. The Seller expressly notes the Buyer has not verified it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket, general disclosure).
- **Buyer wants:**
